cover.headline:
You don't need
heavy weights
to build
[hl]muscle.[/hl]
cover.sub: 49 trained men. 12 weeks. Light vs heavy.

image.label: ai
image.alt: Rack of small and medium hex dumbbells

study.headline: Trained men lifted for 12 weeks. One group went light for 20 to 25 reps. One went heavy for 8 to 12. Every set to failure.
study.note: The heavy group gained more on bench press: 14 kg vs 9 kg.
study.source: Morton et al., Journal of Applied Physiology, 2016

image.label: real
image.alt: Dan doing dumbbell lateral raises by his pool

verdict.headline:
Take every set
[y]close to failure.[/y]
The weight is your call.
verdict.body: Light or heavy, the men who pushed every set to failure grew the same.

image.label: real
image.alt: Dan now, shirtless, hands behind his head, abs visible

items: Pick a weight you can lift 8 to 25 times.
Stop when you can't do one more clean rep.
Want a bigger bench? Go heavier there.
works.headline:
Sore joints?
[hl]Go lighter. Keep growing.[/hl]
works.save: Save this for the next time someone tells you to go heavy or go home.
